Ammonia was first manufactured using the Haber process on an industrial scale in 1913 in BASF's Oppau plant in Germany, reaching 20 tonnes per day the following year. During World War I, the production of munitions required large amounts of nitrate. The Allies had access to large sodium nitrate deposits in Chile controlled by British companies. Germany had no such resources, so the Haber process proved essential to the German war effort. Synthetic ammonia from the Haber process was used for the production of nitric acid, a precursor to the nitrates used in explosives.

The continuous still allowed the alcohol industry to reach new levels of productivity. The still consists of a first column (called the analyzer) in a column still that has steam rising and wash descending through several levels. The second column (called the rectifier) carries the alcohol from the wash, where it circulates until it can condense at the required strength. It behaves like a series of single pot stills, formed in a long vertical tube. The tube is filled with either porous packing or bubble plates. The rising vapor, starts to condense in the cooler, higher level of the column.

A multi-effect evaporator is an apparatus consisting of multiple evaporator bodies linked together in such a way as to allow steam produced by boiling the water in one evaporator to boil water in successive evaporators, with only the first evaporator in the sequence requiring an external heating source. The multi-effect evaporator was invented and patented by Louisiana Creole inventor Norbert Rillieux to increase the efficiency of refining sugar from cane juice. In the early 19th century, the primary method of refining cane sugar from juice was the "sugar train" or "Jamaica train," a typically slave-operated process which relied on pouring hot cane juice reduction through a succession of bowls to increase its evaporation rate. Rillieux's multi-effect evaporator displayed vast improvements in safety, efficiency, and cost over contemporary methods, and to this day remains a staple in industrial-scale evaporation for refining products ranging from cane and beet sugar to sea salt and wood pulp.

A sugarcane harvester is a large piece of agricultural machinery used to harvest and partially process sugarcane. It remains similar in function and design to the combine harvester. These are then deposited into either the on-board container, or a separate vehicle traveling alongside.

A skidder is any type of heavy vehicle used in a logging operation for pulling cut trees out of a forest in a process called "skidding", in which the logs are transported from the cutting site to a landing. However, where forest railways are installed, new rail-based skidders have been introduced that can skid logs to the railroad for loading. With their newly found weakness, we can now take them over and install a new Empire, one that won't discriminate on religion or identity. One that won't exploit the Hausa people.

The Mossi haven't been united for now centuries, and Yenenga's great Mossi Empire is now a distant memory. The legend says the princess Yennenga escaped dressed as a man when she came to the house of a Mandé elephant hunter named Rialé. They had a son named Wédrago who was given that name from the horse that Yennenga used to escape. Wédrago visited his grandfather in Dagomba at the age of fifteen and was given four horses, 50 cows, and a number of Dagomba horseman joined his forces. With these forces, Wédrago conquered the local people, married a woman named Puiriketa who gave him three sons, and built the city of Tenkodogo. The oldest was Diaba Lompo who founded the city of Fada Ngourma. The second son, Rawa, became the ruler of Jatenga. His third son, Zungrana became the ruler in Tenkodogo after Wédrago died. Zungrana married Pouitenga, a woman sent from the king of the Ninisi people, and the resulting intermarriage between the Dagomba, the Mande, the Ninisi, and local peoples became the Mossi people. We must recreate the legend and unite the kingdoms that divide our great people!
Support Muhammad al-Sharif's claim to Wadai

Wadai has been in a power struggle with claimant to the throne Muhammad al-Sharif for the past 3 years, and their army has faced unending battles with thousands of casualties. If we support al-Sharif, who was born in Darfur, we may acquire great influence on the Kingdom of Wadai, which is the key to lucrative trade routes to Tripoli. We would be able to extract tribute from the kingdom by permanently installing al-Sharif as our vassal.

Our Kolak is currently Muhammad al-Sharif, a warlord originating in Darfur that has taken the throne of Wadai thanks to his knowledge of guerrilla warfare and support granted by the Sultanate of Darfur. Using his extensive knowledge of warfare, our Kolak has launched reforms to modernize the army of Wadai with the goal guiding us towards a brighter future as a regional power.

The Fur aren't an united people, and their rulers are weak and pathetic. Though the Sultanate helped Muhammad al-Sharif take the throne of Wadai, we owe them nothing. Being subjugated by Darfur doesn't benefit us, and with our military power they can do little to prevent us from achieving our independence.

The once powerful Songhai Empire was shattered by the Moroccans coming from the other side of the Sahara, armed with guns we now can access. With the decadence of Morocco, their influence in the Niger river has also diminished, and their control is now minimal. The flag of the Songhai flows once again over Gao, and no one can stop our dream of an empire!

The Songhai are weak, and their people are pagan. They are the only people that separate us from the great Sokoto Empire, and we must join forces to expulse the Dendi to Songhailand where they belong, and bring Islam once and for all to the region. We hope Sokoto will help us, or winning the war will be hard, as the Dendi cavalry still remember the days of the Songhai Empire, and their tactics still aren't outdated, regardless of guns.

The Songhai are weak, and their people are pagan. We must join forces with Liptako to expulse the Dendi to Songhailand where they belong, and bring Islam once and for all to the region. Liptako will be launching it first but with our support, or winning the war would be hard for them, as the Dendi cavalry still remember the days of the Songhai Empire, and their tactics still aren't outdated, regardless of guns.

Abu Arish is a kingdom under our influence that once owned the region of the Taiz coast. When we were fighting the Egyptians, the Zaydis took the coast over and came closer to Mecca. We must expulse them from the region and bring them under our thumb!

Despite centuries of European domination of the coast of Angola, the colony's far-flung and vast interior has long eluded our grasp. With growing interest in the territory and recent advances in medicine combating the endemic diseases, we should consider begin extending our rule eastward.
The interior of Angola has been granted to us by the Great Powers, and we now may take it without international complaints -- it is $COUNTRY_ADJ$ territory!

The Lunda Empire, once powerful, is now in decadence. European intervention and the introduction of guns has made its wars more deadly than ever. We are the only state in the region aside from the Great Lakes states that conserve an army capable of conquest, and we could use it to take over Lunda. We once were one of the forming cultures of the Empire, with Chokwes benefiting of the empire, but with its decadence only we can keep intact the greatness of our people!

The Mutapa Empire once spanned all of the Shona peoples, from the coast of Sofala to the highland at the frontier with the Tswana. If we become again the strongest Shona state, we can take the title of the Monomutapa!

The Luvale are a mixture of the Lozi, Lunda, Mbundu and Chokwe peoples, and once belonged to our Barotse state. For these reasons, Luvale will always and has always been an integral part of our kingdom.

The Massangano are a series of kingdoms of partial Portuguese descent that are on the banks of the Zambezi river, from Inhambina to Vila de Sena. Some of them are really powerful, and hold great armies, but claim partial allegiance to our state. If we want to keep our expansion in the region, we must take the Massangano and expand on the Zambezi river. Onwards!
The Matakenya currently own Songo, which is at the end of the land we officially claim for ourselves in the Zambezi River. We need to take such city so we can effectively occupy our claims.

The Berber and Bedouin tribes of the interior claim allegiance to our kingdom, but they keep rebelling and being a weakness to our state. The Europeans use this weakness to attack us, and we must end it via exerting real control over our territory. Centralizing will be a costly and slow process, but it will be worth it.\n\n§RYou need at least 55% civilization progress, the tooltip lies.§W

The Berber and Bedouin tribes of Tarfaya don't claim allegiance to our kingdom, but their northern lands keep rebelling and being a weakness to their state. We must expand to the Draa river and take Guelmim, to find our natural border between the semideserts of Bujadur and the Sahara to the South, and the Atlas Mountains.

The last step to centralize our kingdom is here. The Berber and Bedouins finally are under our state, and Moroccan flags wave over the desert. We have finally centralized Morocco, and brought prosperity to our people. We are now a power to take into account, and colonizing us will be impossible thanks to our great army.
\n\nWith the war at Liptako, our state has changed. Being a part of Sokoto might end up marking our downfall, and independence is tempting. We must hold our breath under the sun of Allah.

\n\nSharif al-Barak ibn 'Abil's Beihan is as powerful as it has been at any point in history. Our plains are fertile, and our power extends to the coast. We hope our kingdom never sinks under the sand of the unending desert.

\n\nFarah Guled, the second Grand Sultan of Isaaq, who lead our forces to victory against the British in the 1827 Battle of Berbera, has passed away. Now, his son, Hassan Farah, has succeeded him as Grand Sultan. The ancient port of Berbera has, in recent years, been fought over between the Ayal Ahmed and Ayal Yunis branches of the Habr Awal clan. As one of his first acts as Grand Sultan, Hassan Farah has brought the warring subclans before a holy relic from the tomb of Aw Barkhadle, one of the companions of the prophet Muhammad, and made them swear to bury all animosity and live as brethren. Thus, Hassan Farah has once again brought peace and good fortune to the Sultanate of Isaaq. May it prosper forevermore!

\n\nOur power is becoming our weakness. Our state has in its borders a trade route which brings guns and other European goods to the center of the continent, and all products are taxed if they pass through us. The Portuguese, though, are trying to centralize their dominions in Africa, and our trade routes might become a target which we can't get rid of. Under this new sun, we hope we shall prevail.

\n\nOral tradition holds that we probably settled along the rainy, hot, and humid river valleys of northern and western Congo in the early centuries of the 1st millennium. We suffered during the active slave capture, trade, and export in the 18th and 19th centuries, where "thousands of Mongo people as captured slaves passed through the Zanzibar route by the Arabs". We must survive in this newfound world of greatness and weakness.

\n\nOur kingdom is between the prosperous Zulu and the warring Xhosa, with our neighboring British nearing in. Our place in the region, though, grants us the control of the trade routes, and we're slowly becoming a truly powerful kingdom, one to not be left behind in history.

\n\nOur people are settled in the wetlands of Mombasa, and our state is between the prosperous Zanzibar and the warring Unyanyembe and Maasai, making us always be under threat. With the Omani and the Europeans encroaching on the coasts, and the Tanzanian kingdoms preparing for a battle to behold, we can only hope our future isn't sentenced.

\n\nWe have survived. Our sultanate has reunited in the face of the Omani, and the Swahili won't be taken as easily as the Arabs think. Our army grows strong, and our navy prepares for battle. The Omani shall be defeated and the greatness of the Kilwa Sultanate restored!

\n\nOur kingdom is between the always-falling Baguirmi and the powerful Kanem-Bornu Empire. Our sphere of influence is nothing compared to Bornu's, and we are de facto their tributary. We must though keep this status or our sovereignty might fall under Bornu, Waddai or even the Adamawa. Our region's future is uncertain, and we must keep all our numbers.

With the slave trade reviving, the search for new slaves has brought the Sahel states to push southwards to previously pagan regions and jungles. With the trade reviving, the states of the Sahel are regaining strength and wielding armies to bring conquest to its neighbors.

The region of Taka, mostly inhabited by nomadic Beja tribesmen, escaped the attentions of the initial 1820 invasion of Sudan, for Sennar was the goal and they did not deviate from the direct route along the Nile. An expedition to the east was indeed suggested to Ismail Pasha, but the Beja had a warlike reputation in Egypt and he decided against it. While Taka paid tribute after the conquest of the Funj Sultanate, this ceased during Khurshid Pasha's term as governor of Sudan in 1838. This prompted the new governor, Ahmad Pasha, to set out with a small army to take control of Taka. When he confronted Sheikh Mohammed Din of the Hadendoa tribe and demanded tribute, he merely produced one tenth of what he had surrendered to Khurshid Pasha. This has enraged Ahmad Pasha, who has now asked us for our blessing to conduct a punitive expedition and found a new fort in the region to collect tribute.

The Mazrui have ruled Mombasa for a century and a half, having used the Portuguese's occupation of Zanzibar to build a base of power. They then annexed Malindi and territories near Pate, and the island of Pemba. In 1823 we managed to expulse them from Pate and take Pemba, but they still hold considerable power. It is time to send them an ultimatum to end their rebellious existance once and for all.
The Subjugation of the Southern Hadendowa

The Hadendowa, a clan of the southern Beja, have increasingly come under our influence. After the founding of Kassala in 1840, the Hadendowa initially refused to pay tribute, until Ahmed Pasha el Menekli, governor of Sudan, cruelly stamped out resistance in 1844. He wantonly slaughtered and mutilated the tribesmen, practising swordsmanship by trying to cut captives in half in one blow. Despite ending Hadendowa resistance, we have only established permanent control of their lands by constructing new outposts in Tokar, Erkowit and Temerein. To the South, the Beni Amer, an unwieldy tribe sandwiched unhappily between the Hadendowa and the Abyssinians, have come to terms with us and begun paying tribute, seeing the enemy of their enemy as their friend. Thus, our line of control has been extended to the banks of the Baraka river.
The Subjugation of the Northern Beja

The last independent Beja clans remained in and around Salala, in the hilly region of the Nubian Desert. Our army has tried multiple times to build forts in the area, but their resistance and the terrain have made these attempts fail. With them having been increasingly encroached on by our army and their sea access being lost to our control of the coast of the Red Sea, these clans have slowly started to pay tribute in a more consistent way, and have finally let our army build a post near Salala, finishing our conquest of the region.

Keren was originally a trading settlement on the Ethiopian frontier, laying on an arid highland plain between the Ansaba and Baraka rivers. The town owes its importance to its position on the trade route between Massawa and Sudan. Typically traded goods include cotton cloth from Sudan and ivory, skins, ostrich feathers and maize from Tigre. While forces have set out from the frontier along the Baraka River and looted Keren and its caravans in the past, our men have now finally permanently occupied it, securing the trade route and logistical connection from Massawa to Kassala for good.

Dallol is located in the Danakil Depression, an extremely hot, dry region rich in geothermal activity, possessing multiple volcanoes rich in sulfur. At 100m below sea level, the Awash River flows to multiple hypersaline lakes at the bottom of the depression. As these seasonally dry up, large deposits of salt are revealed. This salt has been mined for centuries and traded via caravans with the rest of Ethiopia, bringing large tax revenues to those controlling the trade. With our position on the Eritrean coast well established and Dallol under the control of weak, disorganized Afar clans, the valuable salt deposits are ours for the taking. Thus, an expedition has set out from our holdings and taken possession of Dallol.
The Conquest of the Eastern Desert

The Eastern Desert is the part of the Sahara desert located east of the Nile river, consisting of a mountain range which runs parallel to the coast, wide sedimentary plateaus extending from either side of the mountains and the Red Sea coast. While the region had been criss-crossed by trade routes during the Roman period, they fell into disuse and the port cities, including Berenice, became ruins. Between the 7th and 19th centuries, the Eastern Desert was virtually abandoned by all but the nomadic Beja. Now, with the construction of the Suez canal, trade has begun to slowly but surely pick up again, leading to the construction of outposts on the coast.

The Fante Confederacy, a state located in the Gold Coast, only survives thanks to our military support. To increase $COUNTRY_ADJ$ influence in the confederacy, our local administration in the city of Cape Coast has made a proposal to the Fante: We would grant them full protection against the Ashanti Empire in return for significant economic concessions.

The Laikipia peoples live to our north, and are in an inevitable conflict with our kingdom. The Kwavi live in lands that once were part of our kingdom, and occupy them illegaly. We must take their territory and bring them where they belong.

The coast of the Geledi and Hiraabi has been ruled for centuries by Swahili and Mashriqi people, which act almost independently, some of them even having pacts with us for trade or protection. We should capitalize on these weaknesses and claim the Somali Coast!

Hlubi is in a state of chaos. Our inhabitants are under constant threats of massacre by our neighbors, and another scenario like the Mfecane would bring chaos to our region and strengthen Xhosa, where the Mfecane brought immigration which was used for slavery and strengthening its army, which doesn't benefit Mpondo. We hope the Mpondo let us move to Matatiele where we could be a powerful ally...

Some decades ago, our kingdom encompassed all land between the Venda and the Vaal river, and our people were free and prosperous. The Mfecane though made it collapse, and our people had to leave to the mountains to reorganize to conserve sovereignty, With the outsiders having been expulsed from Mosega, we can now claim what our people deserve!

Our people had lived for centuries in Delagoa Bay, and we were forced to the mountains because of the Mfecane, a period of war in Southern Africa which can be situated between 1810 and 1830. Now that we are powerful enough to hold our territory from invasions, we can return to our homeland!
Our kingdom has for centuries been a great state and the powerhouse of the region. Thanks to new weapons coming from Europe, we can now expand in all directions to form the Kaabu Empire.
Our people can't be limited by the Batè! A local named Samori Turé is building an army to bring greatness to the Mandinka peoples and we should join him!

Centuries ago, our people were united under a single banner, the flag of the Jolof Empire. The Jolof Empire fell under internal pressure, and the only kingdom left was the Kingdom of Wolof. With all of the parts of the Empire under our hand, we can now claim its title!
After the fall of Timbuktu, our kingdom became too weak to hold the title of Empire. With our territories regained, we can now become the Bambara Empire again!
With all territories inhabited by Senufos under our banner, we can form the Senufo Empire!
The Akan peoples have been separeted for centuries, and the Ashanti have been keeping it that way with the Fante-Ashanti wars. With our people reunited though, we can now form the Akan Empire.
We have lived in our current territory for centuries, but our peoples have never united. If we unite the lands of the Umbundu, we can finally bring the Umbundu under our flag!
The Luba-Lunda Empire system is obsolete! We should claim all neighboring lands and put an end to this worthless peace. Long live the Lunda Empire!

Mirambo is a Nyamwezi king, ruling over lands bordering Tambora, a vassal state of ours. His territorial claims, though, extend further than our territory, and he has a large army under his fist. If we let Mirambo rule our kingdom, we will be able to rule over the whole of the Tabora plateau!
Claim the Legacy of the Chwezi Empire

The Chwezi Empire was a mythical empire in the oral traditions of our people and existed before the balkanisation of the kingdoms of the Great Lakes. Now that we have subdued all of the other rulers we can claim their legacy!
Another step towards the total liberation of Serbia.
This is a remarkable journalistic feat.
The loss is large, but we shall rebuild.
We must prepare aid for the survivors.

Potash, or fertilizer potassium, has recently been discovered in southern Alsace while searching for coal deposits. \n\nPotash is primarily used in the production of fertilizer, though it can also be used in the bleaching of textiles, the creation of glass, ceramics, and soap.
Let us pray that it does not happen again.
Liptako Has Used the Decision 'Launch a Jihad on Dendi'.
Claim the Throne of the Massina

The Massina and us had the same objective: unite the region under a same banner, one that had Islam in its center and one that would launch jihad at any pagan country that would be in its path. With our occupation of Massina being finished, we can now claim the Massina Throne on the basis of ideals. We have to bring Allah's name to every corner of the continent, and being separated isn't the way we should go.

The Yaka people have been under other states for far too long. Our people have been slaves, we have been borderly, we haven't been important to the great Empires of the region, just a rock to push around. Of course, we will not this continue. With our territories in the West being regained, we finally have the power to be the Empire over the others, a great Yaka Empire. We might, though, see that southwards expansion is what we truly need.

The outsiders, coming from the distant land of Europe and their allies, are getting closer and closer to our lands. The states that divide our people, not the Susu or the Bambara, but the Mande people as a whole, must be united under a single flag to keep off the Europeans and unite in our power. The Mande people must be united, and this will be the first step!
The Lunda people and their neighbors have been disunited for far too long! Our region should be united so we can resist the recent arrival of the Europeans.

Our country is the greatest that it has ever been, but its goal has still not been finalized: uniting the Bemba under a single flag. With the Kazembe out of the picture, now we can start waging war to unite the Bemba, from the Zambezi to the upper coast of the Tanganyika.

The Mfecane brought too much destruction to our region, with a lot of the population migrating to distant lands and losing contact to their mainland, and this one becoming empty of settlements or great kingdoms as it was before, and other countries taking their place but not being able to use the land for farming and falling weak on the steps on the Europeans. We must unite the region in the face of unity, to end this age of darkness.

Our once great empire had been brought into decadence by Portuguese and Omani incursions into our land and commerce empire. With the Omanis displaced from our rightful lands, we can now safely say the Kilwa Empire has returned!

We had had a presence in Nejd for more than 10 years, it being more accentuated in Ha'il. With the Nejdi troops weak and trapped in the east of their lands and the Ottoman Empire in disarray, we should try forcing them to pay us tribute once again.

\n\nThe Imam of Oman has gained influence of power over the last years, having fought a war against the Nejd and gaining positive relations with Abu Dhabi. He has made a campaign to gain followers and allies to centralize Oman under his rule, but they aren't powerful enough to beat us. With troops amounting just outside the city of Dhank, a bloody battle is on the horizon. Should we escalate further and unite Oman and Muscat or back down?

Tarfaya is a coastal city in the coast of the Tekna, south of Morocco, through which caravans go in the route from Timbuktu to Fez. Building a fort in the city could help us trade with the commercial caravans and Mohamed Bairouk.
With our great victory against the Moroccans, we can now recreate the great Kingdom of Sous!

The Egba have been a thorn on our side for now more than a decade, and we have craved their west as much as Ijebu craves Badagry to be theirs. We must regain control over the rebellious provinces of the Egba and partition it under our and Ijebu's rule.

Our King, Kwaku Dua Panin, has suggested to us that we suggest the following pact to the Netherlands so we gain access to western guns: provide Ashanti recruits, a thousand of whom would join the Dutch East Indies Army within a year in exchange for guns. The soldiers would come from Ho, from our local Ewe regiment. With the prospect of army growth, we hope the Netherlands will provide us with what we need.

§RGain 3 infamy§! The countries to our North have repeatedly raided bordertowns for decades, and claim we are a rebellious province of theirs. With the latest raid, we have the casus belli needed to finally bring them down under our rule.

Now that our country has been centralized, we can now officially lay claim to our borderlads, which have been controlled by us sporadically over the last centuries but lost to greater states which now are under us. Long live Kaffa!
Create an Empire with Rabih az-Zubayr

Rabih az-Zubayr is a warlord from Khartoum which has been raiding our borderlands for now quite some time. Our border forces are barely holding them off, but letting Rabih inside our state to pact an union would stop such attacks and unite both armies into one. \n\n§RWarning: You have to merge the brigades that are generated by this decision§W
With Kanem, Bornu and Baguirmi weakening due to the encroachment of the European powers, we can now take them for ourselves.

Our Confederation is in disarray. 20 years ago, we had to leave our capital in Mankhamba due to internal disputes for the throne of the Maravi and the Chewa, and the city and its surroundings have fallen into disuse, with nomadic tribes taking over the region. Now, with the Ngoni taking over our Chewa neighbor in Mkamanga (which once was ours), they have now started raiding our borderlands, and even taken over part of our land and Mankhamba, which we also claim as ours. We have entered into a war we cannot win. Long live the Maravi Confederation!

With the Nguni raids into Maravi proving successful, it gives an opportunity to rise: the slave trade. If we expand our borders towards the coast and the lands of the Maravi, we will be able to rise as the greatest power in the region. Long live the Yao!

The Maravi operated a decentralized political system. With time, the system isolated and weakened the Kalonga, who often had no dependable relations locally. Sometime during the eighteenth century, perhaps due to the growing influence of the Banda clan, the requirement that Undi nominate Kalonga’s successors was no longer enforced which meant that counsellors of the Banda clan at Mankhamba assumed that responsibility. On the surface, it seemed sensible to appoint successors locally. After all, that was how they did it before Undi and Nyangu left. However, times had changed, and this time it did not work smoothly. Its decline there would not have meant much had Mankhamba not been the capital of the Maravi. In this case it did, because it shows that the pottery went into disuse at the site soon after its introduction, an indication that Kalonga and his people abandoned Mankhamba at about that time. Archaeological evidence shows that the site has remained unoccupied ever since.

Throughout the eighteenth century, a growing state of instability characterized the political situation in the Maravi empire. As territorial chiefs became increasingly independent, Kalonga’s grip on power and trade became weak. Other ethnic groups were quick to notice that weakness and they took advantage of it. The best known of those ethnic groups were the Yao in northern Mozambique who developed their own trade routes in the region. They became so successful that, by the 1740s, Portuguese merchants along the Indian Ocean coast recognized them as major traders and some foreign merchants encouraged them to trade in slaves as well. With the decadence of the Maravi, they themselves became the slaves that started to be traded by the Yao int he slave markets of Kilwa and Zanzibar, and with the Portuguese until 1833. We should recover the control over the trades that are conducted throughout the region and reform the Maravi to its greatness.
An outbreak of rinderpest has broken out in this province, and threatens to spread.
An epizootic of rinderpest has started in this province, and threatens to spread.
\n\nAn epizootic of the rinderpest virus is striking Africa, killing the majority of our cattle in $PROVINCE$ and starting famines, which are wiping out sizable amounts of the local population.
With wars all around us finally lowering in intensity, we can now settle in a new capital in Jimeta.
With our newfound power, we can reach the other Fula jihad states of the West and force them to stop their murders and forced conversion of our fellow brothers in religion.
Unite with the Fula Jihadi states
Now that we border each other, we can form an union to create the biggest Western Fula Jihad state to date.
Bornu is too weak to keep us as a vassal, and our kingdom hsa its own sphere of influence and enough manpower to defend against Waddai. We shall revolt and regain what belongs to us.
We have been under Sokoto for too long, which has impaired our ability to lauch jihads under our own volition. We shall leave them and fight for our sovereignty and Islam!
We have been under Kanem-Bornu for too long, which has impaired our ability to defend correctly against Adamawa, under our own volition. We shall leave them and fight for our sovereignty!

In the North we shall find more Hausa states and holdings of the Bornu Emirate, lands which have tried to resist the jihad since its start in 1808. We shall end their resistance and form Emirates in their place!
Fombina, meaning south, used to be owned by the Emirate of Adamawa, now in decadence after we took Yola. As we can consider ourselves to be the successors to their state, we shall claim what is ours.
Expand the Extent of Our Jihad

Our Jihad has been contained for some years now, as kingdoms fortify in their local mountains and mount revolts against our Lamidos. With our newfound power, we can now lay claim to them and make them Lamidos of our own.
Settle for the Arrival of the Mahdi

Usman emphasized to Adama the importance of anticipating the coming of the Mahdi. Usman believed that the Mahdi would emerge from the east and urged Adama to be vigilant for signs of his appearance. Usman had prophesied that the caliphate's reign would last only until the arrival of the Mahdi, within a span of a hundred years. Sultan Bello (second Sultan of Sokoto) further requested Adama to send spies to "south of Wadai and the south of Fur in the direction of the Nile River" so that the people of the caliphate, on the Mahdi's appearance, could "follow him and give him the oath of allegiance."

Since the start of the Fula Jihads, we had to limit our power to the shores of the Chad and the Mandara Mountains, and ally and subsequently fall into the sphere of influence of Kanem-Bornu. Now we should regain our lands to the South, as the jihad states weaken more and more by the day.
Baguirmi is a state to our East, which has never really been friendly to us. If we claim Baguirmi for ourselves, we might end such a danger from our future.
Our kingdom once owned lands to the West of where we're located, but the Fulani Jihads pushed us to the Chad where we are now. We shall return to the lands which were taken from us!
Loango owns part of a region which encompasses most of the modern-day population of the Tio people: Anziku. We should reclaim this territory to reunite our people.
After some bloody battles, we have pacified the Makhzen and instated our rule over Morocco.

The land of Mauritania has been under our influence for centuries, but we have never been able to control the lands directly due to its geography. Now that we control lands to both sides of Mauritania, we can effectively control the region.

Our lands have been occupied by numerous kingdoms, from Darfur to Baguirmi. If we have to become a force to be reckoned with, we have to liberate our neighbor's lands from their oppressors and settle in Wara to create a new empire.
After the defeat of the Diriyah, polities in our north formed confederations of their own, which we rule loosely. We should centralize Ha'il now that we can effectively rule our own territory.

Multiple commissions have tried to determine where our border in Trujillo should fall, but to no avail. With our newfound international support, we have asked a Bourbon king of Spain to arbitrate the issue. After some weeks of discussions, they have ruled in our favor. Viva $COUNTRY$!

Multiple commissions have tried to determine where our border in Nicoya should fall, but to no avail. With our newfound international support, we have been able to form an arbitration committee with representation from Costa Rica and Nicaragua to arbitrate the issue. After some weeks of discussions, it have ruled in our favor. Viva $COUNTRY$!

Chief of Justice of the United States Charles Hughes has proposed to end the Guatemala-Honduras border dispute once and for all, with a commission from Chile, the United States and Costa Rica. If we accept, we might have a higher chance to get what's ours.

We were forced to relinquish our claims to Cauca, the southern regions of Colombia, in the early 1830s. The treaties though were forced upon us and we should not recognize them as legally binding, just justifications for our neighbors' conquests upon our territories.
With the Cauca under our control, we can now reclaim our borders from the times of Spanish colonization, which involves Acre, Cauca and parts of the Upper Amazon rainforest.

The recent discovery of the Bessemer Process has made the metallurgy industry boom in recent months, with factories being built all over Asturias, the Basque Country and Alicante, and iron mines being opened all over the Southwest and Northwest of Spain.

The $COUNTRY$ Confederacy has survived the Fulani jihad thanks to its formidable army, and a lot of bordering territories were lost in the struggle for sovereignty. We must retake them and place our rule over them.
Having centralized our state on Manjacaze, we now can start raiding northly, to get to the Zambezi River and liberate our brothers in the region.

The Gambia colony, first established on James Island in 1815, has grown bit by bit through territorial acquisitions achieved by concluding treaties with the natives. The lower river is now almost entirely under our control and has seen significant economic development through the establishment of lucrative peanut plantations. Neighboring French Senegal has been expanding at a comparatively voracious pace, and our Gambian colonial officials have come to realize that little time remains to expand into upper Gambia before the French take it for themselves.

Manyika is a vassal of ours to the North of our state. It has served its purpose of being a buffer between the Portuguese Zambezi and our empire, but now we can proudly say we can face them without any need to have a buffer.
The Zarma from Dendi have been warriors for centuries, fighting off all foreign powers from their land. We should let some enter our country so they can help us defend ourselves.

King Monze has been gaining followers all over the region and is known as a Prophet of Rain. He is known to have been able to cause rain and cure sickness. We could turn our kingdom into a Theocracy of Rain, Mvwulabwami.
Our cattle have been going down in number due to local plagues, and our people have been massacred to the East. To be able to continue existing, we have to raid the baTawana.

Our raid against the baTawana has been successful, but we can no longer sustain our population. We need to settle somewhere else, somewhere where there's available farmland and the people there won't resist our rule enough to expulse us. We are lucky, the Lozi to our north are weak, and we could annex their farmland and claim their throne.
Grant Equal Rights to the Natives

The Kru, Susu and other people groups that are not Afro-Liberian are more than 90% of the population, but they are discriminated against by our administration. To become a functioning country, we have to grant them equal rights.
The French have been oppressing our brothers for far too long. We should claim the region and restore the Occitan language and culture as one of prestige.

Burgabo is controlled by different Somali tribes, from the Ogaden to the local Boqow. They are unorganized and they rule in a decentralized manner, not correctly controlling the region. With the European powers encroaching on the continent, Burgabo is an easy prey for us, but also the other colonial powers. We should occupy the city and its surroundings, as the holders of Mombasa and Muqdisho have claimed it since the 1820s and we already hold influence in the region.

The Tsonga people have never been united in a single state, but confederations of various sizes. With the Gaza occupying most of the Tsonga region, the Tsonga have started a new nationalistic movement to regain independence and form a new state. As part of the Tsonga people, we could use this opportunity to form an united Tsonga state.

The Kong Empire, named after its capital, also called Wattara Empire after its royal family, has a history that goes back more than 2 centuries. Our peak of power had its borders from the gates of Kumasi and Wadadugu to the approaches of the Niger River. We shall reconquer what's ours!

The Oasis of Buraimi and al-Ain have been under our influence for decades, and they have been taken over in recent years by the Omanis and Abu Dhabians. They constitute a core part of our kingdom and we shall claim them for ourselves!

§RGain 5 infamy§! Our Emir, Dost Mohammad Khan, aims to expand his influence in Bamiyan and Turkistan. He has proposed to send an American mercenary by the name of Josiah Harlan with an army to conquer the region. Josiah Harlan would ally with local forces and occupy the region, which could serve of great purpose to our kingdom. The region that would be conquered is, of course, Kunduz and its vassals, which have been in decline for now quite some time.

§RGain 3 infamy§! Dost Mohammad Khan has managed to regain control over our state, but Bamyan fell to the Hazara in the chaos. We must subjugate the Hazara and reconquer what's ours. §RDeclare war against Hazarajat§!
§RGain 2 infamy§! Dost Mohammad Khan's recent campaign in Hazaristan has thrown the area into chaos. We can use this opportunity to conquer our rightfully claimed lands along the Murghob river.

§RGain 1 infamy§! After Yar Mohammad Khan Alakozai’s killing of Kamran Shah Durrani and usurpation of the throne of Herat, Durrani exiles have fled to the ruler of Taiwara, Ibrahim Khan, and plot to retake the Emirate. This has incensed Yar Mohammad Khan, as he now endeavours to conquer Ghur. We must ready the banners and set off for Ghur before it’s too late! §RDeclare war against The Taymani§!
These are not the attacker's cores
These are not the attacker's cores

Abuja has been resisting attempts to peacefully annexing the local Igala kingdoms, vassals of their respective kingdoms, and Nupeland's borderlands are rebellious and raid our bordering emirates. Those lands clearly have to be brought to our jihad to secure our hold on Ilorin. §RDeclare war against Nupe if it exists§!
Zuru has been resisting attempts to peacefully annexing the local Borgawa kingdoms. Those lands clearly have to be brought to our jihad to secure our hold on Nupeland.

The Northern Bakongo have been oppressed for far too long! The Portuguese and Kongolese have a strong hold on the Southern Bakongo, and have been raiding us for centuries. We should expand southwards and end this menace!

We had been part of the Kilwa Empire, and our lands became very wealthy thanks to newfound trade routes from the interior of the continent, bringing ivory and slaves. Those days have been over for centuries, but we can still bring them back. With our military reformed and the Portuguese pulling back on their control over trade in the continent, we can now retake what's ours.
Our Kingdom has been under the influence of the Aro Confederacy for far too long. We must take the lands of those that have oppressed us and form our own Empire!

Our Confederacy has been weakened by its rivals for far too long. We should bring the lands that we have coveted for far too long under our control and finally reaching our goal of a state for all Ibos!

Our kingdom has been resisting raids by the Igbo and Yoruba for decades, but we once were an Empire spanning lands that are now controlled by our enemies. We should retake our lands and create a kingdom that will never fall!

The European colonial powers have been launching expeditions into the interior of Africa for decades, and our own empire seems small compared to their colonial empires. Abyssinia, a state to our south, is considered internationally to be backwards and easily conquerable by a colonial power. We should have a try at it and expand our empire!

The European colonial powers have been launching expeditions into the interior of Africa for decades, and our own empire seems small compared to their colonial empires. A state to our north is considered internationally to be less backwards and not easily conquerable by a colonial power. We should have a try at it and expand our empire, teaching them who really is backwards!
The $COUNTRY_ADJ$ Expedition to the Eastern Horn

§RGain 5 infamy§! As we have started the expedition to Ethiopia, we have brought attention to Harar and Somaliland, which are unclaimed by the colonial powers. We could try to claim them for ourselves!
Become the Negus of Shewa, Ifat, the Oromo and the Gurage

In 1828, Sahle Selassie had proclaimed himself Negus of Shewa, Ifat, the Oromo and the Gurage, but revolts, disease and famines made him never use these claims. Within our current position, an expansion to the East, South and West can be achieved, bringing prosperity to our great state.

The Funj Sultanate, also called the Blue Sultanate, was ruled by the Nuba Funj people and represented the biggest power in the region before Egyptian encroachment. The Funj converted to Islam some centuries before it fell to Egypt, but nevertheless we can found a state in its place without their mistakes.

Our lands have long been controlled by the Pagans and the Sokoto Caliphate, which have oppressed our people. Now that we're an independent nation, we can use this opportunity to liberate our brothers and sisters and convert the Pagans to God's faith. In the name of the Jihad, long live Ilorin!
Claim the Throne of the Oyo

With most of the Yoruba being now under our control and them converting to Islam, we could claim the Oyo Empire's throne on the basis of the center of Yoruba power having moved to Ilorin. The Pagan Empire shall give way to ours!

§RGain 3 infamy§! The lands to the East of the Ethiopian highlands have long been under the control of Muslim rulers and under the influence of the Ottoman Empire and, more recently, Egypt. With our resurgence as a regional power, we must claim the region for ourselves.
Convert the Lands West of the Senegal to Islam

The Kingdoms of Wolof, Saloum and Sine have sizable minorities and, in certain regions, politheist and/or animist majorities. These kingdoms accept these non-believers, and even lets them form part of their aristocracy. We must stop these infidels from governing in the lands of our neighbors, and convert them to the only, true religion - Islam.

The Oromo people have inhabited the lands of Ethiopia since 400 years ago, and live all around the region, from the land of the Gumuz to Borana and Harar. With our empire growing, we can no longer be considered a Leqa, but an empire for all Oromo.

The Sherbro people inhabit Sherbro Island and the coasts to its north. With our control and influence over the region expanding, numerous Sherbro chiefs have signed treaties with our authorities so we can establish a protectorate.
The Occupation of Karabane and Sédhiou

Karabane and Sédhiou, located on the mouth of the Casamance River, has been claimed by our administration since the 1820s. The commander of our local navy has left for Casamance in search of a suitable site for the future trading post. The village chief of Kagnout has offered us Sédhiou for 196 francs a year, and our navy is starting to build a fort in Karabane to mantain our hold on the region.
Bignona, located north of the mouth of the Casamance River, has been claimed by our administration since the 1810s. We now have an opportunity to occupy Bignona, and we must use it.
The Occupation of the Rio Grande

The River 'Rio Grande' is to the South of Bissau, and is inhabited by non-Papel Bak people. We have tried to occupy it since 300 years ago, but our forts have been destroyed or left to their demise time and time again. With the rest of the European colonial powers starting campaigns around Africa, we should try again and occupy Bolola, founding a new fort in its place.

The Papel Kingdom of Bissau has existed since we started occupying the Guinean Coast, and have been too powerful for us to try to annex them - until now. With the newest technology, we finally have an edge over them, and we can occupy Oio without them burning Bissau to the ground.

The region of Bembe is rich in natural resources, and owned by our ally, the Kingdom of Kongo. Kongo is becoming weaker and weaker with the decadence of the slave trade, and their adaptation to the 'new' trade forcing entire towns to dismantle to turn lands to farming, making their lands unstable. Our settlers in Angola depend upon these natural resources, and we must occupy it to protect our allies in the region.

Since we've started bordering the Rabih, they have raided our border forts and refused to sign any treaties with us. Some days ago, a rogue column started a military expedition to Togbao, one of their forts, to try and bring them to submission, and even with heavy losses they managed to kill 48 of the 51 $COUNTRY_ADJ$ soldiers. With these casus belli, we have more than sufficient evidence to prove that Rabih must be pacified.

§RGain 2 infamy§! §R(Pay 50,000¤)§! With the European powers encroaching on their territory in multiple fronts, the Southern Azande try to resist occupation. If we fund a big enough expedition, we might be able to make them do otherwise, and sign a protectorate...

The Maasai, Nyamwezi and Ujiji peoples between Zanzibar and Lake Tanganyika are being encroached from the West by colonial expeditions. Their territories have lots of natural resources, and conquering them brinds us the ability to expand more inland, and block the British from obtaining a connection between their colonies.

§RGain 2 infamy§! §R(Pay 50,000¤)§! With the European powers encroaching on our former Regency, Algiers, we must find a way to help them resist the invasions and free the Arab world from Christian attacks. Now that we have secured a route for our resources and armies to be sent to Algeria, we can start helping them.

The Libyan Desert has numerous oasis, and has been used for centuries to trade with the Sahel, to the other side of the Sahara. We have influence over most of the oasis in the desert and we might be able to take over their administration, as most of the trade routes there begin in our territory, and the word of Senussi has been heard to the other side of the desert.

Our zawiyas, or monasteries, extend all around the Western Arab World. The ones in the Central Sahara and Libya, though, are becoming more and more economical, educational, and military centers, with buildings teaching tactics, fighting skills and using muskets. We may control parts of the Desert between Tobruk and Waddai, that's not where our influence ends. We could use this to our advantage, and unite the Central Sahara against the foreign powers of the North.

The Trekkers had founded a town named Ohrigstad in the heart of baPedi territory, isolated from Potchefstroom or Zoutpansberg. The town failed due to a malaria epidemic, but Lydenburg was founded some tens of kilometers to the South by the same settlers the next year. The baPedi have become more and more distrustful about the expanding control of the Boers over the region, and it has started fortifying the neighboring lands, almost encircling the town. The settlers have asked our militias for help, but a war against baPedi wouldn't be beneficial to our economy. We could pact with them so they cede the region to us for §R50,000¤§!, but if we do not gather these pounds we will have to fight.

The baPedi and Venda have for centuries lived in the Drakensberg Mountains and the Lowveld, Bushveld and Highveld, but with our arrival to their territory some have escaped to the Drakensberg, where they reorganized and from where they launch raids into our territories. To pacify our borderlands, we'll need to claim the Drakensberg Mountains.

Zanzibar has been under Oman for far too long. The Mazrui have strived to unite the coast under its people, and with the final conquest of the last holdouts we can now proudly say we not only claim Zanzibar, we now are Zanzibar. Long live the Zanzibari Coast!

The Kilwa Coast is controlled by different coastal tribes, from the Zaramo to the local Swahili. They are unorganized and they rule in a decentralized manner, not correctly controlling the region. With the European powers encroaching on the continent, Kilwa is an easy prey for us, but also the other colonial powers. We should occupy the city and its surroundings, as the holders of Zanzibar and Sudi have claimed it since time immemorial and we already hold influence in the region.

With our current position in the Drakensberg Mountains, we could consider claiming the entire mountain chain, becoming a state powerful enough to face the powers of the region from the peaks of the Great Drakensberg.
Claim the Lowveld, Bushveld and Highveld
We have managed to form the $COUNTRY$, and we now are a power to be reckoned with. As we tower over the plains that surround us, we could integrate them into our great state.
Send an Expedition to the Dogon

§R(Pay 60,000¤)§! The Dogon have lived in the Bandiagara Escarpment for centuries, isolated from the rest of the continent in the small valleys with plentiful water. With our power growing all around their territory, we might want to fund an expedition to centralize and annex Dogonland to our state.

§R(Pay 50,000¤)§! Samo is a region that was once part of the Mossi Kingdoms, but control became decentralized, and now the region is governed by the 3 Mossi clans of the northwest. With our power growing all around their territory, we might want to fund an expedition to centralize and annex Samo to our state.

Kebbi is the last fully-independent Hausa state that hasn't been conquered in our great jihad, and it is as close as it can get from Sakkwato. A slim majority of the Kebbi farmers have still ignored the Word of Allah, and its administration does nothing to change this. To fix this issue and stop the infidel Kebbi government from continuing to opress its Muslim population, we must occupy it and form a new entity, the Gwandu Emirate in its place.

The Chewa people's origins are in Malambo, in what is now inhabited by the Luba, and we were forced to emigrate by ethnic groups further north in the 9th century. In the 15th century, we formed the Maravi Confederation in the northern regions of lake Malawi, and from there we became the most powerful country in the known world. If we had not been expelled from our homeland, we would probably have not suffered through what we have, but it also means we have a claim to what is now the Lunda and Luba empires, and as we do we shall overcome our enemies and someday become the Lunda Empire!

Our state currently consists of numerous, highly-autonomous states that mostly do not accept our rule, thus our inability to totally control our state. If we fulfill the conditions in the tooltip - just broke the fourth wall-, we might be able to centralize our state. \n\n§RYou need at least 25% westernization progress, the tooltip lies.§W

Our state currently consists of numerous, highly-autonomous states that mostly do not accept our rule, thus our inability to totally control our state. If we fulfill the conditions in the tooltip - just broke the fourth wall-, we might be able to centralize our state. \n\n§RYou need at least 25% westernization progress, the tooltip lies.§W

\n\nOur people have escaped from the South and the Mfecane, but our fight continues. The Gwangwara, a Ngoni group from the Gaza Empire, have also been forced to escape north, which we shared, and were part of our kingdom until 3 months ago, when a battle broke out between our king M'Mbelwa's forces and the Gwangwara, and we've managed to force them to move east to Songea, south of Uhehe.

We have been able to establish a kingdom in the heart of the continent, far from any great enemy and with a superior army in professionalism and arms. With control over the North of the Chewa Sea, we should be able to establish our Empire, as great as ever!

§RGain 2 infamy§! Our state has been confined to the Futa Jallon Mountains for decades, and our neigbours to our North and South - the Mayo and Neola Tenda and the Solimana: the last Jallonke state from the people that had humiliated our people for centuries-. To bring the jihad to our Animist neighbors, we must move to bring them into our state: the Tenda would accept being a puppet and ceding Fulbe-plurality regions, but Solimana will refuse any pact...

Gao had been the great capital of the Songhai Empire and the Dendi province of the Mali Empire, but since the city has lost power and fallen to little Songhai city-states under constant fear of Tuareg raids. We must occupy Gao to bring them into centralized control and bring Gao to what it once was.

The Ghana Empire is the first empire we know of in African pre-colonial history, existing from the third century to the thirteenth century, and the people that ruled the empire are the ancestors of the Soninke of Kaarta, Xaaso and Solimana. It is our duty to conquer our lost lands and recreate the Ghana Empire!

The Ghana Empire had good trade relations with the peoples of the West, where now the Wolof, Western Fulbe and Serer live. The local kingdoms aren't too hostile to us, but to conserve our trade routes and bring new greatness to our Empire we must bring it under our control.

The regions of Dendi and Kebbi had been enemies to our Empire in the past, but they were strong enough to keep off our armies and keep control over their lands and the trade routes from the Akan gold mines. Wee can revert this error today now that we're the most important power in the continent.

The Mossi Empire is under repeated attacks by the colonialist powers of the sea, and our region isn't unified enough to resist them. To do so, we must expand in all directions in the spirit of Yennenga's expansion to Wagadugu.

Mali had a coastline in the Gambia and Senegal rivers to our West, where the Wolof and Western Fulbe people live. It is an integral part of our Empire, and thus we must move to conquer it and bring it under our control.
Recreate the Empire of Great Fulo

The Empire of Great Fulo was a Pulaar Fulbe empire that spanned the Senegal and Gambia rivers, and resisted multiple Islamic jihads by Muslim Fulbe rebel militias until 1776, when it was overthrown by the Imamate of Tooro. With control over the region restored, we can recreate the Empire of the Denianke.

\n\nThe Portuguese Royal Family had had for a while a monopoly over the ivory trade to Angola, and they were our biggest partner, so we were forced to lower prices and the trade became unprofitable. Now that their monopoly is no longer an issue, we can now recover our control over the trade and increase our production.

§R(Pay 30,000¤)§! European traders have had commerce with our merchants for centuries at this point, a reality from which we can't readily escape. To keep our administration profitable, we could potentially fund expeditions to hunt ivory and conquer the Marrevoni Lomwe Makwa to our North to establish rubber plantations for the Europeans to purchase.

§R(Pay 30,000¤)§! The lands of the Hassane have long been divided between emirates and clans, some of them being Brakna, Shratit, Abkak Taganit and Adrar. In our current position, we would be able to conquer the first three for a cost of §R30,000¤§!, bringing newfound unity to our great people.

The Kingdom of Antankarana has long been independent from our rule, and claims to be linguistically and ethnically different to our state. We must show them the error in their ways, and integrate them into a great and prosperous Imerina!

§R(Pay 70,000¤)§! Sahle Selassie's reign has been full of famines, revolts and epidemics, but he has been trying to round up support for westernizing reforms, both for the people and for expansion of his kingdom. The only negative are its increasing costs, he asks for §R70,000¤§! to be able to start his reforms.
Our country is in an all-out debt crisis, and we must act to fix this hole in our budget.

British so called 'missionaries' have been settling on our land and teaching their mistake of a religion to people in our cities, and teaching them how to read and write in their language as a way to 'civilize' us. This is clearly an act of aggression and it must be dealt with accordingly.
Our relation with the Witu Emirate has been growing for decades, and with the other powers encroaching on their sovereignty, it might be time to help them survive in this cruel world.

The Hehe have grown in power in southwestern Tanganyika for decades, and now they're a power to be reckoned with. As they're one of the last roadblocks to our expansion in the region, we should launch an invasion to end their kingdom once and for all.
Unite the Turtle Islanders by Force
We have no other choice but to invade our neighbours and expand to face the American oppression of our people once and for all.
We must move to defend from the foreign invaders that occupy our lands.

The Sultanate of Sohar has been an independent Sultanate for decades, since the Wahhabis invaded our homeland and our grip over the western territories became weak. It is ruled by the remainder of the Yarubid family, the dynasty of Oman in the early 18th century, and might be plotting to overthrow our state. Should we annex Sohar once and for all, these issues would be sorted out.

Our ruling family was once part of the Yarubids, the dynasty that ruled Oman until the mid-18th century, when it was lost to Muscat. Now, with Muscat under control, we can restore our rightful rule over Oman!
End the Assimilation and Conversion Policy
§GLose 5 infamy§! Our hold onto the Horn of Africa is firm, and we've pacified the polytheists into submission. It might be time to truly settle down and start a new golden age of progress.

§RGain 5 infamy§! Adal comprised all lands between Zeyla, Aussa and Harar, and were the center of the Adal Sultanate centuries back. The Sultanate was an example of the greatness of our people, and controlling it again we're able to claim its revival.

§RGain 10 infamy§! It is our duty and that of the Adal Sultanate to convert the infidels to the only, true religion. As a first step, we must start incursions into their territory and win the favor of the Oromo people, some of which are true Muslims.

§RGain 15 infamy§! The Abyssinians have been infidels for too long - they have resisted conversion for centuries and only defeated the first Great Adal through treaties with the once-powerful Portuguese. Now that we control the southern hills and mountains of what they call their homeland, it's time to declare a new empire and bring Abyssinia under our control once and for all. For Islam!
Declare the Caliphate of the Adal
§RGain 5 infamy§! Adal is now the greatest power in the recent history of Islam, and we must act that way. To encourage further conversions into Islam, it's time to declare a Caliphate in all rights.

The Tibetan Plateau is inhabited by various Tibetan peoples, most of them not sedentary, and has been for millenia. With the westernization of our bureaucracy and army, we are now able to control them.

Our days as a fully-independent nation are numbered. With the British at our doorstep and our enemies defeated, we might wanna offer something to the British they can't deny - becoming their ally in the region as a princely state, in exchange of control over Kashmir, now under their control.
Establish a Puppet State in Ladakh
§RGain 2 infamy§! To keep expanding our domains to the North, we must bring Ladakh under our control and claim it as part of our great state.

§RGain 5 infamy§! As the rightful claimants to Ladakh, we must bring under our control the lands they lost to Tibet in the XVII-XVIII centuries and bring our country to control both sides of the Himalayas!

§RGain 5 infamy§! The Sikh Empire had for decades ruled Jammu, but a rogue governor took Jammu for himself in the early 1820s, and the territory was lost. Today we're back in a position to establish lasting control over Jammu and its surrounding territoris once and for all.

The Northern Arapaho have lived for centuries in the Black Hills, a land now mostly inhabited by the Lakota group of the Dakota. We have been allied from time to time with them, but the presence of our brothers isolated from us in their land is becoming more and more untenable. We must reestablish control over the Black Hills and become the great state we used to be!
Launch a Punitive Expedition against the Cherokee

§RGain 2 infamy§! The Cherokee have recently moved into Nabiti in their strategy to escape the American efforts to deport them to the Indian Territory. They raid our border towns as much as the Comanche and bring destruction everywhere they go. We must pacify this enemy and send them to their homeland in Tha'tse.
Claim Kabylia, the Chotts and Qusantina

§RGain 2 infamy§! When the Regency of Algiers collapsed, we lost most of our control over the lands east of Kabylia, and wars against the imperial powers of Europe stopped us from reclaiming them. Now that we have the power necessary to launch an invasion east, we should claim those lands for ourselves once more.

§R(Pay 49,000¤)§! The lands of the Regency of Algiers have been part of our realm for centuries, but we had had to cede autonomy to local polities due to constant internal conflicts. Now that our state is more or less stable and we hold enough power to centralize, we must do so!

\n\nThe forces of the Riograndense Republic, led by Italian revolutionary Giuseppe Garibaldi, with help from the local population, conquered parts of Santa Catarina, establishing a new republic.
You are at war for Arauca.

In 1826, the at the time President of the United Provinces of the Río de la Plata and Unitarian Bernardino de la Trinidad González Rivadavia drafted a constitution to centralize La Plata once and for all. The Constitution was sanctioned on the 24th of December of 1826, with it soon proving itself unpopular among the provinces and reigniting the civil war between Unitarian and Federalists. Rivadavia's Constitution would soon die on its craddle, with the civil war it ignited leading to the Federalist takeover of Buenos Aires. \n\nNow that we don't have to worry about Federalist savages anymore, our condition is more favorable, letting us adopt once again the 1826 Constitution, letting the document once again be our binding constitution.
Our lands in Jawiya remain exposed to raids from tribes in the interior, but our technology had not been enough to establish control over the deserts around the Euphrates, until now.
\n\nOur army has established a fort in the lower Euphrates river to better control the Anizah tribe in al-Jazira, and with it the raids to our newfound control over Syria will be secured.

\n\nWith our war against the Ottomans, the Anizah have taken control of our fort in the Euphrates, named Dayr az-Zour, and restarted raiding to ash-Sham. We'll someday retake it and finish off the raiding once and for all.

The Ottoman Empire is searching for an excuse to annex us, and our autonomy is slowly being stripped from us. We must declare our independence and protect the sovereignty of our state once and for all!

Muntafiq is an Arab Emirate in the coast of the Persian Gulf, where they control Basrah and the surrounding wetlands and deserts. They have tried multiple times to free themselves from our rule, and they are a roadblock to our great empire's centralization. We must end their autonomy and bring Basrah under our direct rule.

With our victory in the Cabanagem, we have the upper hand in any potential border negotiations with Brazil. If we were to fund a diplomatic expedition to Rio de Janeiro, we'd be able to potentially force Brazil to rescind their claims on Pará and Rio Negro. §R(Pay 20,000¤)§W

The actions of the Ka'aretama so called 'republic' have gone too far. They are assimilating our people and destroying the natural order of the Amazon rainforest, completely against our terms in a previous treaty. We must claim the lands of the Amazon rainforest to stop these heinous acts at once!
Encourage Settlement in the River Valleys

§R(Pay 40,000¤)§! The genocidal acts of the Empire of Brazil and its predecessors forced most of the people that once lived near the Amazon River to migrate elsewhere into the rainforest. With our newfound control over the river valleys and technology, we can recolonize the regions that were stripped from us and bring stability to the region once and for all.

§R(Pay 50,000¤)§! There are many people in our nation that are interested in learning their local Amerindian language, be it to better communicate with their local Amerindian community or to continue their family's language tradition if they never passed it down to them for fear of being repressed by the Brazilian regime and others of its kind. It is only fair that we start a program to facilitate education in these languages and increase proficiency in them across our population.
With the final occupation of the Brazilian lands, we can finally reform Brazil how it was supposed to be - without slavery and open to everyone, with no oppression related to race or religion.
Claim The Lands of The Nheengatu, Cocama and Northern Amazonians

§RGain 10 infamy§! (§RBefore 1851 will cause a Quechua revolt in Peruvian lands.§!) The Amerindian peoples of the Andes and its foothills have been oppressed for far too long! We must claim the lands from the Northern Andes to the Amazon River for ourselves to free our brethren from their cruel occupation forevermore.
Claim Mato Grosso and Moxos and Chiquitos

§RGain 10 infamy§! The lands around and east of the Madeira River are the cradle of the Tupian languages, and many Amerindian nations there remain relatively independent. In contrast, west and south from it, the colonial nations continue to oppress tens of thousands of Amerindians even with our pleas to grant them autonomy. Claiming these lands is the only sensible outcome to react to these injustices.
Claim The Lands of the Jê

§RGain 12.5 infamy§! The Jê and the Tupinamba have never been allies, but this is now changing. Our move for a united Amerindian nation in Pindobetama has caught the attention of numerous Jê nations, and our success has only emboldened them more to join our cause. Today we can safely say an alliance between the Jê and the Tupinamba, though once thought of as impossible, has been forged.
